newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala prisoners protest for better conditions.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala prisoners protest for better conditions.

text.p: More than 700 inmates in Guatemala's largest prison began what they called a peaceful protest on Monday, saying they would block entry to prison workers and calling for improved conditions.

"We have a peaceful attitude. There is no violent pressure," prisoner Guillermo Donis, serving 12 years for murder, told Reuters. He spoke through the perimeter fence at the Pavon prison about nine miles (15 kms) southwest of the capital.

Prison director Lorenzo Castillo told reporters that as a precautionary measure he had ordered employees not to report to work on Monday after the prisoners sent a note to administrators saying they would block entry to the jail. He said the prisoners had food inside and could feed themselves without the presence of prison employees.

The prisoners distributed a list of demands including work and study programmes, improved water, electricity, health, telephone and food services, an audit of the prison system and the prosecution of corrupt employees.

Recent investigative reports by the Siglo Veintiuno newspaper detailed widespread corruption in the prison administration. The reports exposed poor living conditions as well as lax security in prisons, where convicts have easy access to weapons and luxuries such as cellular phones.

Donis said the prisoners demanded the presence of Pablo Monsanto, a commander of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit, to help with negotiations. The URNG signed a peace accord with the government last month, ending 36 years of bloody civil war.
The director of the Guatemalan prison system, Carlos Villacorta, briefly entered Pavon in the morning but told reporters he was not able to negotiate an end to the protest.
